name: Genome Nexus
description: We need a comprehensive, single-source system called Genome Nexus to provide fast, automated, and high-throughput annotation and interpretation of genetic variants in cancer. This system should integrate data from various existing resources, including databases that convert DNA changes to protein changes, predict the functional effects of protein mutations, and offer information on mutation frequencies, gene function, variant effects, and clinical actionability.

<p dir="auto">Genome Nexus, a comprehensive one-stop resource for fast, automated and
high-throughput annotation and interpretation of genetic variants in cancer.
Genome Nexus integrates information from a variety of existing resources,
including databases that convert DNA changes to protein changes, predict the
functional effects of protein mutations, and contain information about mutation
frequencies, gene function, variant effects, and clinical actionability.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Documentation 📖</h2><a id="user-content-documentation-" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Documentation 📖" href="#documentation-"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">See the <a href="https://docs.genomenexus.org" rel="nofollow">docs</a></p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Alternative 1 - run genome-nexus, mongoDB and genome-nexus-vep in docker containers</h3><a id="user-content-alternative-1---run-genome-nexus-mongodb-and-genome-nexus-vep-in-docker-containers" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Alternative 1 - run genome-nexus, mongoDB and genome-nexus-vep in docker containers" href="#alternative-1---run-genome-nexus-mongodb-and-genome-nexus-vep-in-docker-containers"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">First, set environment variables for Ensembl Release, VEP Assembly, location of VEP Cache, and species (since a mouse instalation is supported). If these are not, the default values from <code>.env</code> will be set.</p>
<p dir="auto">The reference genome and Ensembl release must be consistent with a version in <a href="https://github.com/genome-nexus/genome-nexus-importer/tree/master/data">genome-nexus-importer/data/</a>.
For example <code>grch37_ensembl92</code>, <code>grch38_ensembl92</code> or <code>grch38_ensembl95</code>:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="export REF_ENSEMBL_VERSION=grch38_ensembl92"><pre class="notranslate"><code>export REF_ENSEMBL_VERSION=grch38_ensembl92
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">If you want to setup Genome Nexus for mouse, also set the <code>SPECIES</code> variable to 'mus_musculus'. Also see the <a href="https://github.com/genome-nexus/genome-nexus-importer/blob/master/docs/setup-genome-nexus-mouse.md">docs</a> to create a mouse database.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="export SPECIES=mus_musculus"><pre><span class="pl-k">export</span> SPECIES=mus_musculus</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">If you would like to do local VEP annotations instead of using the public Ensembl API, please uncomment <code># gn_vep.region.url=http://localhost:6060/vep/human/region/VARIANT</code> in your <code>application.properties</code>. This will require you to download the VEP cache files for the preferred Ensembl Release and Reference genome, see our documentation on <a href="https://github.com/genome-nexus/genome-nexus-vep/blob/master/README.md#create-vep-cache">downloading the Genome Nexus VEP Cache</a>. This will take several hours.</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# Set local cache dir
export VEP_CACHE=<local_vep_cache>

# GRCh38 or GRCh37
export VEP_ASSEMBLY=GRCh38"><pre class="notranslate"><code># Set local cache dir
export VEP_CACHE=<local_vep_cache>

# GRCh38 or GRCh37
export VEP_ASSEMBLY=GRCh38
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Run docker-compose to create images and containers:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="docker-compose up --build -d"><pre class="notranslate"><code>docker-compose up --build -d
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Run without recreating images:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="docker-compose up -d"><pre class="notranslate"><code>docker-compose up -d

highLevelGoals: To obtain fast, automated, and high-throughput annotation of genetic variants in cancer by integrating diverse genomic and proteomic data sources.
To understand gene function, predict the functional effects of protein mutations, and analyze variant effects to advance scientific understanding in cancer biology.
To leverage integrated data on mutation frequencies, gene function, and variant effects to explore and validate scientific hypotheses related to cancer mechanisms.
To receive accurate and clinically actionable interpretations of genetic variants to guide evidence-based clinical decision-making for cancer patients.
To utilize comprehensive variant interpretation, including clinical actionability, to develop optimized and personalized treatment strategies for cancer patients.
lowLevelGoals: The Researcher submits a batch of genetic variants to the system for automated annotation.
The Researcher specifies which genomic data sources should be used for the variant annotation process.
The Researcher specifies which proteomic data sources should be used for the variant annotation process.
The Researcher retrieves the comprehensive annotation results for a previously submitted batch of genetic variants.
The Researcher queries the system to retrieve detailed functional information for a specific gene.
The Researcher submits a protein mutation to the system to predict its functional effects.
The Researcher requests an analysis of the functional effects associated with a specific genetic variant.
The Researcher queries the system to retrieve mutation frequencies for a specific gene across various cancer types.
The Researcher retrieves integrated data (mutation frequency, gene function, variant effects) for a specific genetic variant.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors "Researcher" and "Oncologist" are relevant to the system's purpose of annotating genetic variants in cancer. However, the description emphasizes that the system is a "single-source system" that "integrates data from various existing resources." This implies a significant interaction with external data providers or databases (e.g., those converting DNA to protein changes, predicting functional effects). While these might be considered external systems rather than human actors, in GORE, the entities providing the data or the system administrators maintaining the integration are often considered actors if they have goals or constraints. More importantly, the description mentions "clinical actionability," which strongly suggests that clinicians (beyond just oncologists, potentially including genetic counselors or pathologists) are key users. Additionally, the system is described as providing "fast, automated... annotation," which might imply an API consumer or another software system as an actor if it's intended for integration into other workflows. However, the most critical omission is likely the **System Administrator** or **Data Curator** who manages the integration of the various existing resources, as maintaining the "single-source" nature requires active management of these integrations. Without an actor responsible for the data integration aspect, the model is incomplete regarding the "how" of the system's operation.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The provided high-level goals are well-aligned with the software description and the defined actors. They correctly capture the core functionalities: automated annotation, functional interpretation, and clinical actionability. The goals are functional (focusing on the 'what' and 'why' for the users) and do not contain non-functional requirements (like specific speed metrics or security protocols) or out-of-context features. There are no contradictions or major omissions regarding the primary purpose of the system as described.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-structured, correctly mapped to the high-level goals, and align with the system description. They appropriately distinguish between the Researcher's need for high-throughput data integration and hypothesis generation, and the Oncologist's need for clinical actionability and treatment planning. The goals are functional, specific, and cover the key aspects of the Genome Nexus system (annotation, interpretation, data integration, and clinical application). There are no obvious omissions or contradictions.
